correctness.rationale: The Cartesian adjacency rule gives twelve distinct equal-sized closed neighborhoods of five vertices, so these are exactly the maximal faces. An independent set-based reconstruction tests subsets of the 12-vertex universe for containment in one of them and gives all 250 nonempty faces and vector (12,54,112,60,12). At each pivot, toggling that vertex defines disjoint candidate pairs, so successive removal within a stage makes the same matching as simultaneous removal. For all three specified pivot orders the independent code obtained 114 pairs and critical vector (1,0,21,0,0), and used depth-first cycle detection on all 744 directed cover incidences, orienting just the paired ones upward. Finite discrete Morse theory therefore gives a CW complex with one vertex and just 21 two-cells, all attached to the vertex by constant maps; its ordinary homotopy type is the asserted wedge, proving the integral homology and fundamental-group conclusions. Finite-field ranks are not needed for the strongest conclusion.
residual_risks: This matching is checked for the specified graph only. It establishes a nonequivariant homotopy equivalence, not an equivariant statement or a theorem for other cycle lengths.

evidence: The clique-fiber theorem requires a triangle- and four-cycle-free base and gives the stable S^1 wedge 4n two-spheres for C_n and width 3.
The square-completion theorem instead requires the entire graph to be triangle-free; the target has triangle fibers. Matsushita's product example has two complete factors, and C4 is not complete.
broader_coverage.reasoning: No verified broader theorem here has hypotheses which include the target graph and complex.

evidence: The stable clique-fiber argument uses unique bridging pairs. Opposite C4 vertices have two common neighbors, so that argument does not specialize.

The out-of-scope substitution n=4 in the stable formula would incorrectly retain a circle and give only 16 spheres; the exact Morse matching instead decides both the missing circle and the number of spheres.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The result is not mechanical substitution or computation of a known complete-factor case. It resolves the exceptional closed-neighborhood instance, with the homotopy equivalence rather than just ranks.

evidence: It is the closed neighborhood complex for the Cartesian product, equivalently the vertex-centered closed Čech construction at unit radius under the cited conventions. Scale two in the intrinsic nerve uses balls of radius 2/2; Matsushita's graph-vertex metric Čech notation uses radius 1.
An open Lovász neighborhood deletes each center; the graph-square clique complex instead uses pairwise distance. Neither defines these same facets.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Changing the radius convention without changing the closed neighborhoods is equivalent; changing open/closed or replacing the common center condition with pairwise proximity is not.

value.rationale: This is the first base cycle precisely excluded by the natural longer-cycle theorem, where its bridging hypothesis fails. The computation decides that the stable fundamental circle disappears and provides the exact replacement homotopy type with a small replayable Morse certificate, rather than a homology-only sanity check.
residual_risks: The contribution is the specific motivated boundary case, not a new all-width or all-cycle theorem.
